desc:
A binary tree is a binary search tree (BST) if for every node all values in its left subtree are strictly smaller than the node's value and all values in its right subtree are strictly larger. The empty tree and a single node are BSTs.

Every node of a given binary tree roots a subtree made of that node and all its descendants. Return the number of subtrees that are valid BSTs. Every leaf counts, and the whole tree counts if it is a BST.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree on the left: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

For tree = [10, 5, 15, 1, 8, -1, 7] the answer is 4: the leaves 1, 8 and 7, and the subtree rooted at 5 (children 1 and 8). The subtree rooted at 15 is not a BST since its right child 7 is smaller than 15, and the root is not a BST because it contains that subtree.
constraints: Every tree array follows the encoding above exactly (valid level-order, no trailing -1)
hints: Testing each node separately by running a full BST validation on its subtree works, but may be quadratic on tall trees.

For a node to root a BST both child subtrees must be BSTs, the largest value on the left must be smaller than the node, and the smallest value on the right must be larger. What two numbers do you need from each child subtree?
Compute, bottom-up and once per node, whether the subtree is a BST together with its minimum and maximum value. Add one to the answer whenever the flag is true.
editorial: The classic validation passes down lower and upper bounds, but here the question is asked for every subtree, so a bottom-up formulation is better. For each node keep three facts about its subtree: is it a BST, its minimum value and its maximum value.

A node with value v roots a BST exactly when its left child (if any) roots a BST with maximum < v and its right child (if any) roots a BST with minimum > v. In that case the subtree minimum is the left child's minimum (or v if there is no left child) and the maximum is the right child's maximum (or v). If the node does not root a BST, mark it so; its ancestors then fail too, because a BST can only contain BST subtrees.

Nodes are processed from the last in level order to the first so children are ready before parents. Each node is touched once: O(n) time and space. Strictness matters: equal values on either side make the subtree invalid.
